proof_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x, and set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer such that m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m from the right-hand inequality gives x - m < 1. Since m = floor(x), this is exactly x - floor(x) < 1. Because x was arbitrary, the inequality holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Use the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) <= x < floor(x)+1. The upper bound immediately yields x - floor(x) < 1.
